findings.title: XSS protection now depends on deprecated environment options
findings.problem: The installed Starlette constructor explicitly deprecates extra environment options, including this `autoescape=True` argument. The previous code configured escaping directly on the Jinja environment. Escaping still works today (a script payload rendered as escaped text), but the change makes that guarantee depend on continued support for the deprecated forwarding path. Production installs unpinned dependencies with `pip install .`, so the lockfile does not stabilize this behavior. If forwarding lapses, escaping depends on library defaults; losing it would expose interpolated search names and details in `partials/search_log.html:19` to script injection.
findings.fix_hint: Restore the explicitly configured `jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True)` and pass it through the supported `env=` argument.

members.title: Diff reverts the just-made jinja2.Environment fix, undoing documented autoescape remediation
members.problem: This diff changes `templates = Jinja2Templates(env=_jinja_env)` (with an explicit `jinja2.Environment(..., autoescape=True)`) back to `Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)`. `git log` shows the immediately preceding commit (e11187e, "fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape") made exactly the opposite change, with the message: "Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions. Pass a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead, which is the supported API." This working-tree edit silently reverts that fix back to the pattern the prior commit explicitly rejected.

members.title: Diff reverts autoescape back to Starlette's deprecated **env_options path; HTML escaping (protection against injected scripts, XSS) now depends on the installed Starlette version, and the module can crash at import
members.problem: This diff exactly reverses commit e11187e. That commit's message says "Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions", and it fixed this by passing a preconfigured jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True). The locked Starlette version (uv.lock: starlette 0.52.1) still accepts the old call, but the installed starlette/templating.py:92-96 shows it raises a DeprecationWarning ('Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.'). The Dockerfile (line 31: `pip install --no-cache-dir .`) ignores uv.lock, and pyproject.toml declares `fastapi` with no version pin. So the production image installs the newest FastAPI/Starlette. If Starlette has dropped **env_options there, as the earlier commit says, `Jinja2Templates(directory=..., autoescape=True)` fails with a TypeError when routes.py is imported and the app never starts. Even where it still works, the explicit autoescape guarantee now runs through a deprecated path instead of an Environment configured directly. Starlette's _create_env does default autoescape to True today (templating.py:114), but that is a library default, not a guarantee in this code. If escaping lapses, Radarr/Sonarr titles and other external strings rendered in templates could inject script. pending: confirm whether the Starlette version pip resolves in the Docker build still accepts **env_options.

members.title: Reverts HEAD's fix and goes back to the deprecated Jinja2Templates env_options passthrough on an unpinned fastapi/starlette
members.problem: This diff exactly reverses commit e11187e ('fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape'). That commit moved routes.py to the supported `Jinja2Templates(env=...)` API. In the installed starlette (.venv/.../starlette/templating.py lines 92-95), any `**env_options` such as `autoescape=True` raises `DeprecationWarning: Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.` The constructor still works today, and `_create_env` already sets autoescape=True by default (line 114), so the kwarg is also redundant. But pyproject.toml lists `fastapi` with no version bound, so a future starlette that drops `**env_options` would raise TypeError when routes.py is imported and take down the whole web UI. Commit e11187e's message says this has already happened on newer versions.

members.title: Revert puts XSS autoescaping back on Starlette's deprecated env_options path, and fastapi is unpinned in Docker builds, so a future Starlette release can stop the app from starting
members.problem: This diff exactly reverts commit e11187e ("use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape"). Before it, autoescape=True was set on a jinja2.Environment that the app built itself, which is Starlette's supported API (env=). That guarantee held no matter which Starlette version was installed. Now autoescape=True goes through Jinja2Templates(**env_options). In the installed Starlette 0.52.1 (.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/starlette/templating.py:92-96) that path raises DeprecationWarning("Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead."). It still works for now, through _create_env (templating.py:107-116), which also calls setdefault('autoescape', True). However, pyproject.toml:15 lists `fastapi` with no version bound, and the Dockerfile:31 runs `pip install --no-cache-dir .` without uv.lock. Each image build therefore pulls the newest Starlette. When Starlette removes **env_options, the call at routes.py:45 raises TypeError when the module is imported. triggarr/__main__.py, scheduler.py and both test modules import routes.py, so the whole web UI and daemon would fail to start. If Starlette instead keeps the keyword but ignores it, HTML escaping (the XSS control) depends only on a library default. Today the escaping comes from a deprecated path plus a library default, not from code the app controls. pending: the date or version when Starlette drops env_options is not confirmed. Today's behaviour (escaping on, warning emitted) was verified in the installed 0.52.1.

members.title: Autoescape guarantee downgraded from explicit jinja2.Environment to deprecated Starlette passthrough, risking stored/reflected XSS on a routine dependency bump
members.problem: The diff reverts `templates = Jinja2Templates(env=_jinja_env)` (with `_jinja_env = jinja2.Environment(loader=..., autoescape=True)`) back to `templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)`. I read the installed starlette source (triggarr/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/starlette/templating.py, v0.52.1, matching uv.lock) directly: passing `autoescape=True` this way goes through the `**env_options` kwarg path, which the code explicitly flags with `warnings.warn('Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.', DeprecationWarning)`. It still functions today only because `_create_env` happens to `setdefault` autoescape onto the Environment it builds. This is exactly the fragile mechanism the prior commit (e11187e, 'fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape') removed, with the commit message stating in this same repo: 'Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions.' fastapi/starlette are unpinned in pyproject.toml ('fastapi' with no version spec), and this repo's own git log shows automated dependency-bump PRs for starlette (e.g. 'chore(deps): bump starlette in the uv group'), so the next routine bump can land on a Starlette release where this deprecated passthrough is dropped or ignored, silently disabling autoescape across every Jinja2 template this app renders.

members.why_it_matters: Templates in this app (e.g. triggarr/templates/partials/app_card.html rendering app.instance, app.tag_warnings[].tag sourced from Radarr/Sonarr API responses, and triggarr/templates/settings.html rendering user-editable config values) interpolate dynamic data with no `| safe` filters anywhere in the templates directory, meaning autoescape is the only XSS defense for all of them. This diff doesn't disable escaping under the currently pinned starlette==0.52.1, but it replaces an unconditional guarantee with one that depends on a deprecated code path this exact repo has already seen broken by a Starlette upgrade once before.
members.fix_hint: restore the explicit jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader(str(TEMPLATES_DIR)), autoescape=True) passed via Jinja2Templates(env=_jinja_env), as the prior commit e11187e did, instead of relying on Jinja2Templates' deprecated **env_options passthrough
